timelines.coverage_note: Reviewed chronology covers Facebook's first company-designed data center, its launch and Open Compute disclosure, subsequent campus buildout, the 2021 two-building expansion, and scrutiny of the associated tax incentives.

events.title: Facebook breaks ground on its first custom data center
events.summary: Facebook began construction in Prineville on its first company-designed and company-owned data center.

sources.title: Facebook Begins Building Its Own Data Center In Oregon
Meta's Prineville Data Center info sheet

events.title: Facebook launches Open Compute from the Prineville design
events.summary: Facebook publicly released hardware and data-center designs developed for Prineville and created the Open Compute Project around them.

sources.title: Facebook Launches Open Compute Project

events.title: Facebook launches its Prineville region
events.summary: Facebook described Prineville as its newly launched third data-center region and its first built from the ground up around a custom facility and server design.

events.title: Meta announces buildings ten and eleven
events.summary: Facebook announced two more buildings totaling 900,000 square feet, projecting an 11-building, 4.6-million-square-foot campus and more than $2 billion in investment.

sources.title: Our Prineville Data Center is growing again!

timelines.coverage_note: Reviewed chronology covers Google's first owned data center, the fourth-building expansion, the 2021 incentive and water agreements, the public-records litigation, disclosure of water use, and the completed aquifer-storage project. Competing claims about water need and benefit remain attributed.

events.title: Google opens its first owned data center in The Dalles
events.summary: Google opened the Oregon facility that began its shift toward building and operating its own large data centers.

sources.title: The Dalles, Oregon data center location
Top-secret Google data center almost completed

events.title: Google begins building a fourth data center
events.summary: Google's location history records the start of construction on the campus's fourth data-center building.

sources.title: The Dalles, Oregon data center location

events.title: Wasco County approves a new strategic investment agreement
events.summary: The county approved a long-term partial tax-abatement agreement supporting another Google data-center development after public hearings.

sources.title: Wasco County approves Google agreement

events.title: City approves a contested expansion water agreement
events.summary: The Dalles approved an agreement under which Google would transfer water rights and fund roughly $28.5 million in utility projects while securing supply for two more planned buildings.
events.scope_note: Supporters described system-wide benefits; critics argued the vote lacked essential disclosure about existing Google water use.

sources.title: The Dalles approves controversial water deal with Google
The Dalles approves Google water agreement

events.title: The city sues to withhold Google's water-use records
events.summary: After the district attorney ordered disclosure, The Dalles sued The Oregonian/OregonLive to prevent release of annual water-use data that the city and Google treated as a trade secret.

sources.title: Oregon city fights to keep Google's water use secret
Google uses a lot of water in The Dalles. Soon we'll know how much.
sources.publisher: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press

events.title: Settlement ends the water-records lawsuit and forces disclosure
events.summary: The city agreed to release Google water-use records from 2012 through 2021 and pay the news organization's legal fees; Google then said it would stop treating site-level water use as a trade secret.

sources.publisher: Circuit Court of Oregon and the parties

sources.title: The Dalles settles Oregonian lawsuit, releases Google water records

events.summary: Google and The Dalles announced completion of an aquifer storage and recovery project intended to increase long-term municipal water capacity.

events.summary: OPB revisited two decades of city records and challenged official claims about how Google's expansion relates to reservoir and utility planning.

timelines.coverage_note: Reviewed chronology covers Boydton's announcement, repeated capacity expansions, the 2014 discovery and later removal of a historic Black cemetery, generator permitting, the Circular Center, and the current operating permit. The cemetery account is attributed to investigative reporting and includes Microsoft's response.

events.title: Microsoft establishes its Boydton data-center campus
events.summary: Microsoft announced a latest-generation data center in Mecklenburg County with an initial investment commitment of up to $499 million.

sources.title: Microsoft Picks Virginia for Major Data Center
Celebrating 10 years in Boydton, Virginia

events.title: Microsoft announces a $150 million second data center
events.summary: Microsoft announced a second Boydton facility adding roughly 21 megawatts of electrical capacity beside the initial campus build.
events.scope_note: The amount and capacity were announced expansion figures.

sources.title: Microsoft Builds Two-Headed Data Center in Feds' Backyard

events.title: Two more Boydton buildings are announced
events.summary: Microsoft announced another roughly $348 million expansion involving two data-center buildings at the Mecklenburg County campus.
events.scope_note: The investment was an announced commitment.

sources.title: Microsoft To Build Two More Data Centers in Virginia
Southside Planning District Commission 2014 Annual Report

events.title: A historic Black cemetery is found and later relocated
events.summary: Investigative reporting found that developers discovered a cemetery during 2014 site preparation and that 37 graves were later excavated and consolidated without direct notice to known descendants.
events.scope_note: Microsoft said Mecklenburg County followed applicable law; descendants and archaeologists criticized the identification, notice, excavation, and reburial process.

sources.title: Historic black cemetery was moved for Microsoft data center in Virginia

events.title: State holds a hearing on 48 additional diesel generators
events.summary: Virginia DEQ held a public hearing on an amended major-source permit that would add 48 emergency generators and increase permitted diesel throughput.
events.scope_note: Permit limits describe maximum authorized operation, not routine annual emissions or fuel use.

sources.title: Public Hearing — Microsoft Corporation East Coast Data Center

events.title: Virginia announces Boydton's fifth expansion
events.summary: The governor announced a $251.6 million Microsoft expansion and 44 additional jobs, identifying it as the campus's fifth expansion.
events.scope_note: The amount and jobs were announcement-stage commitments.

sources.title: Governor McAuliffe Announces 44 New Jobs and More than $251 Million Investment in Mecklenburg County
sources.publisher: Commonwealth of Virginia via Mid-Atlantic Broadband

events.title: Microsoft opens a Circular Center at Boydton
events.summary: Microsoft opened a facility designed to process up to 12,000 decommissioned servers per month for reuse and recycling.
events.scope_note: This is a materials-reuse milestone rather than a power-generation project.

sources.title: Microsoft datacenters in Virginia

events.summary: DEQ issued a superseding construction and operating permit covering numerous named Boydton building phases and their backup-power equipment.
